lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF7 — Paying Taxes: Taxes, Take-Home Pay, and Your First Forms
lessonRef.title: Comparison and analysis: integrating PF1-PF7 into one plan

objective: Assemble a single fictional annual plan that carries income, taxes, spending, saving, credit, investing, and protection together, and check that it balances.
scenario: A fictional worker earning $44,000 builds one simulated annual plan. The tax schedule is the simplified fictional one used in this unit and every figure is invented.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional income and plan figures in these directions

tasks.directions: Gross income is $44,000. Under the fictional federal schedule, taxable income is gross less a $9,000 standard deduction, then 10% on the first $10,400 of taxable income and 12% above it. Payroll tax is 7.65%, state income tax 4.25%, and city income tax 1%, all charged on gross with no deduction.

prompts.text: What is the federal income tax?
What do payroll, state, and city taxes come to together?
What is take-home income for the year?

tasks.directions: The plan allocates take-home pay as follows: essential spending $21,600, debt repayment $2,640, emergency reserve $2,400, long-horizon investing $3,600, and insurance premiums $1,860.

prompts.text: What do the five allocations total?
How much of take-home pay is unallocated?
What percentage of gross income goes to tax? Round to one decimal place.

tasks.directions: Write the plan up as one page.

prompts.text: Present the plan and show how each of the seven topics from this course appears in it. Say what the $2,232 unallocated should do, and name the one line you would cut first if income fell 10%.

remediation: Use the fictional scenario and work one graded prompt at a time. For each number response, copy the given fictional quantities into integer cents, choose the operation the wording calls for, calculate, and check the result with an inverse operation or estimate. For each written response, make a claim and support it with at least one detail from the fictional scenario. Use these steps to check the method while keeping every final result in your own response.
extension: Rebuild the plan on $39,600 of gross income, keeping the reserve and insurance lines intact, and state which two lines absorbed the fall.

targetConcepts.meaning: Taxes fund public purposes and use rules that define a base, rate, timing, and responsibility.
A simplified tax calculation applies only to the fictional jurisdiction, year, and assumptions stated.
Withholding is a prepayment estimate; it is not automatically the final tax owed.

evidencePurpose: Develop and apply tax purpose, taxable bases, and stated tax rules through the existing fictional lesson work, including calculation where relevant and evidence-based decision reasoning.

conceptExplanation.title: Understand tax purpose, taxable bases, and stated tax rules
paragraphs: Taxes fund public purposes and use rules that define a base, rate, timing, and responsibility.

A simplified tax calculation applies only to the fictional jurisdiction, year, and assumptions stated. In this lesson, the learner uses the provided fictional facts about integrating PF1-PF7 into one plan; no real household information belongs in the work.

Withholding is a prepayment estimate; it is not automatically the final tax owed. The usable process is: Identify the fictional tax base and included items. Apply only the stated rate or brackets in order. Account for stated credits or withholding after tax is computed. Round at the declared point and label the result.
relationship: Identify the fictional tax base and included items.
Apply only the stated rate or brackets in order.
Account for stated credits or withholding after tax is computed.
Round at the declared point and label the result.
conceptExplanation.commonConfusion: A marginal rate applied to one bracket is not automatically the effective rate on all taxable income.
conceptExplanation.conditionsAndLimits: Use only the stated fictional facts, time period, rate meaning, fees, taxes, timing, rounding, goals, and constraints. The result is education for this scenario, not individualized advice.

calculationPolicy.currency: USD where a prompt states USD
calculationPolicy.operationOrder: Use the learner-visible scenario order and apply only the stated inflows, outflows, rates, fees, taxes, interest, deposits, charges, or payments.
calculationPolicy.rounding: Treat exact-cent results as exact. When a prompt requires rounding, round only at its explicitly stated point and to its stated unit; use half-up for cent rounding unless the prompt declares another rule.
calculationPolicy.taxAssumptions: Use only the fictional jurisdiction, year, base, rates or brackets, deductions, credits, withholding, caps, and order stated in the learner scenario.
calculationPolicy.normalization: Follow each prompt’s requested unit and precision. Dollar and cent forms are equivalent only when the adult authority declares that normalization.
permittedTools: calculator when listed in lesson materials or task directions
calculationPolicy.verification: Protected fixed authority remains adult-only and is independently recomputed or comparison-derived from integer cents, basis points, exact rationals, or validated decimal strings. Binary floating-point output is never final authority.

workedExamplePolicy.separationRule: The model uses different fictional people, amounts, wording, and decision conditions from protected independent and mastery work.

workedExamples.title: Worked example — tax purpose, taxable bases, and stated tax rules
workedExamples.fictionCue: Every person, amount, product, institution, and rule in this example is invented for instruction.
facts: No deductions, credits, or withholding; round once to cents, half up.
workedExamples.goal: Compute the tax under this fictional flat-rate rule.
workedExamples.relevantInformation: Use only the listed fictional facts and conditions; do not substitute real household information.
workedExamples.method: Identify the fictional tax base and included items. Apply only the stated rate or brackets in order. Account for stated credits or withholding after tax is computed. Round at the declared point and label the result.
steps: Represent $300.00 as 30,000 cents and 5.00% as 500 basis points.
Amount after this tax: 30,000 − 1,500 = 28,500 cents, or $285.00.
Check: $15 is one twentieth of $300, which matches 5%.
workedExamples.interpretation: The $15.00 result belongs only to the stated simplified instructional model.
workedExamples.reasonablenessCheck: Check: $15 is one twentieth of $300, which matches 5%.
workedExamples.tradeoff: Changing the taxable base, jurisdiction, year, bracket rule, credit, or withholding changes the result.
workedExamples.limits: The conclusion applies only to the stated fictional facts. A changed rate, fee, time, rule, goal, constraint, or risk can change it.
workedExamples.calculationAuthority: All USD calculations shown here are written as integer cents. Percent rates, when used, are integer basis points divided by 10,000; stated rounding is half up at the declared line only.

guidedPracticeContract.learnerAction: Select and carry out the relevant operation with the fictional quantities, then interpret the result.
guidedPracticeContract.supportBeforeAction: Vocabulary, labelled facts, the approved separate model, and an empty organizer may be used only outside protected attempts.
guidedPracticeContract.feedbackAfterAction: Check for the observable confusion: A marginal rate applied to one bracket is not automatically the effective rate on all taxable income.
guidedPracticeContract.expectedEvidence: A learner-produced calculation or comparison plus financial meaning in the learner’s own words.
guidedPracticeContract.fade: Step cues and parallel models end before independent or protected evidence.

independentScenarioContract.independentBoundary: Use only the stated fictional facts and declared tools. No completed step, selected option, decisive justification, or protected result may be supplied.
independentScenarioContract.responseForm: mixed exact calculation and written reasoning
independentScenarioContract.freshness: The protected case keeps the target but changes facts, constraints, timing, representation, or alternatives from the worked model.

decisionReasoning.gradeBandDemand: Test assumptions, compare interacting constraints, defend a conditional decision, and identify residual risk.
framework: Identify fixed facts, constraints, and assumptions.
Compare relevant benefits, costs, risks, and opportunity costs.
Use a calculation only when it answers a decision question.
Defend a conditional choice and name a changed fact that could change it.
decisionReasoning.neutrality: More than one conclusion may be defensible when priorities differ; scoring follows relevant evidence and internal consistency, not an adult lifestyle preference.

masteryRule.independenceRule: Worked examples, completed organizers, answer-bearing hints, or decisive feedback invalidate the protected attempt; use a fresh case after support.
masteryRule.evidenceRequired: Correct or acceptably normalized fixed work plus aligned financial interpretation or decision reasoning.
masteryRule.decisionRule: Mastery is decided only by the aligned adult-only authority for the named evidence lesson; completion alone is not mastery.

remediationRoutes.observableSignal: A marginal rate applied to one bracket is not automatically the effective rate on all taxable income.
remediationRoutes.alternateExplanation: Use a labelled fact–rule–result–meaning organizer. Separate what the fictional case states from what must be calculated or judged, then connect the result back to the stated goal.

parallelWorkedCase.title: Alternate model — tax purpose, taxable bases, and stated tax rules
parallelWorkedCase.fictionCue: This is a different invented case, not a protected task answer.
facts: Fictional taxable sale: 8,000 cents; invented sales-tax rate: 4.00%; tax is rounded once to cents.
parallelWorkedCase.representation: Write each money amount as integer cents, label the goal and constraints, and keep assumptions beside the calculation or comparison.
steps: Label this as an invented instructional rate, not current tax advice.
parallelWorkedCase.check: Reverse the arithmetic where possible and confirm that the conclusion uses a stated goal or constraint.

remediationRoutes.guidedRetryRule: Use the alternate representation on a different fictional case, require the learner to complete the decisive step, and fade labels after the attempt.
remediationRoutes.freshMasteryRule: Use a fresh protected case after support; do not count the parallel model or supported retry as mastery.
